title: Comparing Fractions Worksheets: Unlike Denominators
intro: Teach unlike-fraction comparison using equivalent fractions or a benchmark.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Keep the whole the same and compare each fraction with one-half or rename both using a common denominator.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12

Renaming changes the number and size of the pieces together. It does not change the amount of the whole represented by either fraction.

Ask your student

Are the pieces in these two fractions the same size?

If your student needs help

If the student compares numerators alone, draw both fractions on matching strips.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set has six distinct ordered pairs. Equality is possible but not guaranteed in every set. Mixed numbers, zero, and fractions greater than one are outside this practice. The answer key supplies the comparison sign; an adult can review the child's explanation separately.
